_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's tech-meetup-announcement template (studio/templates.py make --spec). Its film is projects/tech-meetup-announcement (local: the hosts' logos are third-party), pulled with studio/template_from_film.py from kitcut.ai film studio-20261002-181257-gpnrli: AI Agents Speakeasy, LiveKit x Modal's happy hour at LA Tech Week 2026 (Wed Oct 14, 6-9 PM, Santa Monica; tech-week.com), its look measured off livekit.io and modal.com. v3 (2026-10-02) replaces v1-2, an art-deco speakeasy the owner rejected as cringe: a one-event theme had become every remake's costume. Proven pixel-identical to the film; the dotted x between logos then given air (gap 1.9 h, was 1.2).
title: Tech meetup announcement
description: A 30-second announcement for a tech meetup, music only, in the look developer-tools companies post: a black page, light grotesque type, the hosts' own accent colours on one word a line, small mono labels, hairline rules. The series label types on and the hosts' logos land with a dotted x between them, the meetup's name rises in large light type, who it is for, what it is not and what it is (up to three numbered lines), a spec-table card with the date, time and place and the date lit in a dot matrix, and the logos again with the call to RSVP, the link and the hashtag.
author: KitCut
example: Our Rust meetup in Austin, Thursday Nov 12, 6-8 PM at Capital Factory, talks and pizza. Our logo is attached.
brief:
A 30-second meetup announcement with no narration, on a 112 bpm clock (a bar 2.14 s) in six scenes: open (logos, 0-4.3 s), name (4.3-8.6), who (8.6-12.9), offer (the not-line and the beats, 12.9-19.3), facts (the spec table and the dot-matrix date, 19.3-25.7) and end (25.7-30). A scene with nothing to say (no audience, no not-line and no beats) is left out by the code and the rest close up: then move the sfx.json cues of the scenes after it by the same bars (score.json runs the whole 30 s either way). Keep score.json and sfx.json otherwise.

THE LOOK IS THE HOSTS': black page, Inter in light weights, IBM Plex Mono labels, hairline rules, colour on ONE word a line (the hosts' accents). Never add ornaments, glow, illustrations or a theme from the event's name -- a 'speakeasy' or a 'summit' is a word on the page, not a costume. Take the accent colours from the hosts' own sites or logos.

Everything the film says is content.json (SK.DATA.content). series: the tech week, conference or series with its year, as the event writes it ('LA Tech Week 2026'), set as a mono label; "" for none. hashtag (or ""). name: the meetup's name as its page writes it, set large (fitted; two lines past ~24 characters) and nameAccent: ONE word of it to colour. format: the kind of evening in a few words ('Invite-only happy hour', 'Two talks + pizza'). hosts: 1 to 3 {name, logo, col, k}: logo is a picture key of a logo that reads on black -- call template_pictures(logos=[...]) with the hosts' logos in order and use the "light" keys it answers (logo-1-light...); col is the host's own accent colour; k scales a logo whose ink is optically small (1 = as is; ~1.2 for a mark with a lot of air). audience: who it is for, one sentence up to ~60 characters, and audienceAccent: one word of it. not: one short line the event itself says it is NOT ('No demos. No pitches.'), "" when the page says nothing like it -- never invent one. beats: 0-3 short lines of what happens (up to ~24 characters), from the event's page; the last word of each is coloured. date: {weekday 'Wed', month 'Oct', day 14, monthNum 10} (the dot matrix shows month.day). time ('6–9 PM'), place: the neighbourhood or the venue and city (up to ~30 characters), never a private address the event hides. cta: how to sign up, as the event says it ('RSVP on Luma', 'Free · Register on Meetup'); link: the shortest address that opens the event, without https:// (up to ~30 characters). labels: the small mono labels (translate them for another language).

Find the facts on the event's own page (Luma, Partiful, Meetup, Eventbrite, the host's site, a tech week's calendar) and the hosts' logos on their brand pages (the picture tool); never invent a date, a time, a place or a beat.
